page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-8 is an arm64-based server instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 1 thread per core. Powered by the 3.0 GHz ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor, this instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1D cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

In benchmark testing, the c4a-standard-8 demonstrates strong memory and compression performance. It achieves a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3082.2 and a strong read-only large-block memory bandwidth of 198.51 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression at 32.3 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.14 GB/sec, and Geekbench text processing at 2491.0 also rank in the strong tier. However, cryptographic performance is a notable tradeoff, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the weak tier at 1665.96. Other metrics, including Geekbench multi-core and Redis SET operations, fall within the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4a-standard-8 leverages the ARM Neoverse-V2 architecture to deliver high memory bandwidth and efficient single-threaded execution without the overhead of hyperthreading. This makes it a viable option for workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores and high memory throughput. Recommended workloads include text processing, software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight database operations. It is less suited for heavy cryptographic tasks or large-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by its weak prompt processing speed on 7B models.
